key_insight: Varying interfacial tension only mildly changes the overall crown height and spreading diameter in drop-film impacts, but it strongly alters the internal crown composition.
engineering_relevance: The study helps predict splash morphology in immiscible-fluid impacts and shows how FS3D can be efficiently run on modern APU-based supercomputers for large-scale direct numerical simulations.
method: Used FS3D direct numerical simulations to isolate interfacial tension effects in drop-on-film impacts.
Performed grid independence checks using compound crown height as the resolution criterion.
Validated against experiments for impact morphology and crown heights, then extended the setup to interfacial-tension variation.
evidence_signal: The simulations matched experimental crown heights well in water-drop-on-oil-film validation, and scaling tests showed 4x speedup on MI300A APUs with good strong scaling to 4 APUs and linear weak scaling to 512 APUs.
watch_item: Internal crown structure is sensitive to interfacial tension, so conclusions about splash composition may depend on accurate interface modeling and sufficient resolution.
paper_title: The Role of Interfacial Tension in Direct Numerical Simulations of Drop-Film Interaction for Immiscible Fluids
